subject: Regulated deal: capacity sourcing, ops checklist and commit timeline
messages:
From: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@medsyn.com>
To: priya_natarajan@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@medsyn.com, John Patel <john.patel@medsyn.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood hosting options + initial demand profile

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Procurement asked me to put our expected usage and some operational constraints in writing so you can assemble pricing and a capacity plan. High level:

- Workload: regulated PHI processing for triage and clinical summarization, mostly chat/QA and embeddings for search.
- Traffic profile: 2 spike windows (09:00-11:00 and 18:00-20:00 ET) with P50 concurrent token throughput ~350k/day and 99th percentile burst up to ~1.2M tokens/hr.
- Latency target: median <150ms for chat; p99 <700ms.
- Security: must run in isolated tenancy (no multitenant GPUs), customer-managed KMS, audit log retention 7 years for export.
- Procurement ask: compare Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) vs Private deployment (VPC/on-prem) — include cost delta, procurement timeline, and the operational handover checklist.

Attached is a rough demand spreadsheet. Can you confirm next steps and what you need from legal/infra?

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Liu
Director, Clinical AI
Medsyn Health

--
Attachment: medsyn_demand_profile_Q3-Q4.xlsx (spreadsheet, 210KB)
From: priya_natarajan@redwood.com
To: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@medsyn.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 24 Aug 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood hosting options + initial demand profile

Hi Sarah — great to get the numbers. We ran a quick pass with the team and sketched three recommended paths (summary below). I'll assemble formal pricing and a checklist but wanted to confirm assumptions before we produce docs:

Assumptions to confirm (quick):
- Average request length: 120 tokens; avg response 250 tokens.
- Model family: you want a 70B LM for clinical summarization and an embedding model for search (we'll propose quantized variants).
- Data residency: US-only, single region (us-west-2) with a DR replica in us-east-1.

Three options (high level):
1) Private (VPC) — customer-managed control plane in your VPC, fully isolated GPUs (hard tenant), HSM/KMS in-customer. Pros: maximum isolation, easiest for audit; Cons: longer procurement (infra + network), higher ops handoff.

2) Dedicated (Redwood-managed reserved GPU pools) — single-tenant GPU pools (soft pin), Redwood manages control plane but we provide connectivity options for KMS keys and SAML. Pros: faster onboarding, predictable monthly pricing, Redwood handles upgrades; Cons: constrained if you require air-gapped HSMs or physical isolation.

3) Hybrid commit (Reserved + Burst) — a smaller reserved Dedicated commit for steady-state + short-term Private bursts (or cross-zone burst pools) during spikes. Pros: balances cost and compliance; Cons: complexity in routing and fallbacks.

Key questions for us: can you confirm whether an on-prem HSM is a hard requirement or if customer-managed cloud KMS with dedicated HSM key wraps is acceptable? Also, confirm whether 7-year log retention must live in your tenant or can be exported to your archive bucket.

Next steps: we'll produce a two-page procurement comparison, a recommended commit tier (tiling by 80GB H100 equivalence), and a runbook for the handover. Target to share docs by Thu EOD.

- Priya
Priya Natarajan
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: priya_natarajan@redwood.com, Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@medsyn.com>
Cc: karthik_iyer@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 25 Aug 2027 08:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood hosting options + initial demand profile

Adding engineering notes on sizing and ops implications:

- Hardware: for the given peak profile we recommend sizing reserves in equivalent H100-80GB units. Peak token throughput implies ~8 H100-equivalent GPUs for steady-state headroom; bursts can be handled with a 4-GPU burst pool (on-demand) or cross-zone reserve.
- Packing: clinical transformer decodes are high for KV cache; assume 1.5x memory overhead vs vanilla decoder-only transformers. Use packing ratio of 0.7 for mixed-request batching during spikes.
- Quantization: 4-bit INT4 for embeddings and a mixed INT8/FP16 for the summarization model offers ~2.4x cost reduction with minimal MRR quality delta — include quantized variants in model catalog and fallbacks.
- Canary & Rollout: recommended 2-week canary (10% traffic), step up days 3 and 7, with automatic fallback to hosted baseline model if error rate or latency exceeds thresholds for 3 consecutive windows.
- KMS: we can integrate customer KMS but on-prem HSM requires Private — otherwise we can support an external key wrap policy with dedicated HSM in our cloud.

Operational asks for procurement package: link to SOC2 and audit artifacts, sample network ACLs, SLA language for p99 and credit calculations, and a rollback runbook. I'll attach a draft capacity worksheet and the commit options pdf.

Marissa Cole
Principal Deal Engineer
Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: redwood_commit_options_v2.pdf (9 pages), kms_arch_diagram.png (diagram)
From: John Patel <john.patel@medsyn.com>
To: priya_natarajan@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@medsyn.com, Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@medsyn.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Aug 2027 10:21:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood hosting options + initial demand profile

Thanks — this is helpful. A couple of clarifications from procurement/infra: 

1) HSM requirement: our security team prefers an on-prem HSM for wrapping keys used on clinical workloads; cloud HSM with customer KMS is a secondary option but will require additional attestation. Is there an incremental cost/lead time estimate for Private vs Dedicated to support on-prem HSM?

2) SLA: procurement asked us to quantify expected p99 latency and corresponding credits if SLOs are missed — please include sample language we can circulate.

3) Runbook: we need the ops handover checklist and escalation matrix (names + contacts) if Redwood is operating Dedicated capacity.

If you can give numbers (capex/opex breakdown, commit terms: 6/12/24 months, and estimated lead time) we can move to internal signoff.

Best,
John
Head of IT Operations
Medsyn Health
From: priya_natarajan@redwood.com
To: John Patel <john.patel@medsyn.com>, Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@medsyn.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 29 Aug 2027 16:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood hosting options + initial demand profile

John / Sarah — thanks for the clarifying questions. Quick answers and action items attached:

Summary answers:
- Lead time: Dedicated reserved pools (Redwood-managed) — 3–5 weeks after contract + infra checks; Private (customer VPC with on-prem HSM) — 10–14 weeks (network, HSM validation, on-site provisioning when needed).
- Incremental cost: Private carries a ~35–55% premium vs Dedicated (varies by HSM model and support tier). We included a sample cost table in redwood_commit_options_v2.pdf.
- Commit terms: we support 6/12/24 month reserved tiers. For your profile we recommend a 12-month Reserved64 baseline + 4-GPU burst pool on-demand for peak windows. This maps to an estimated steady monthly OPEX equivalent of the Reserved64 tier (numbers in doc).
- SLA language: see attached draft clause — p99 target, measurement window (30 days), credit formula (pro-rated based on % of time SLO missed). We'll work with procurement to finalize.
- Ops handover: see attached runbook checklist; primary escalation: Marissa (deal eng), Karthik (SRE), Vivek (account lead).

Open items for Medsyn to confirm:
- Acceptable KMS path (on-prem HSM vs cloud HSM + attestation).
- Whether DR replica must be physically isolated or can be logical separation in a secondary Redwood VPC.
- Approval timeline for 12-month commit and whether procurement needs a vendor security questionnaire returned before PO.

Next: Marissa and I will drop a concise procurement packet (pricing, runbook, SOC2 artifacts, network ACL template) in the Drive by Mon EOD. Can we schedule a 30-minute procurement review early next week? Proposed times: Mon 09:00-10:00 ET or Tue 14:00-15:00 ET.

Thanks — Priya
Priya Natarajan
Senior Solutions Lead, Redwood Inference
